newsitem.title: UK: UK Fossil Fuel Levy raises 844 mln stg in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: UK Fossil Fuel Levy raises 844 mln stg in 1996/97.

text.p: Britain's Fossil Fuel Levy, a tax raised from the revenues of electricity generators to subsidise the nuclear industry and renewable energy, raised 844 million stg in 1996/1997, Director General of Electricity Supply Stephen Littlechild said on Monday.
"In November I was able to reduce the levy from 10 percent to 3.7 percent for the remainder of the financial year," said Littlechild.

"This resulted in 844 million stg being collected from licensed electricity suppliers from their revenues for supplying electricity in England and Wales - 633 million stg between April and October and 211 million stg between November and March."
Between April and October, some 90 percent of the Levy went to nuclear generation, with the rest going to renewables energy schemes.
From November to March, some 77 percent went to nuclear generation, with renewable generation again taking the remainder.
The Levy was cut further to 2.2 percent from April 1997.
